title: Pauri 21, sound: teerath tap
tomorrow: Pauri 21, meaning: when was the world made

cards: A checklist for being a good person. Go on the big trip to the holy place. Fast, or give something up.
Be kind. Give to charity, and give generously. Most people would call that a solid list.
Now imagine someone reading your list, nodding, and saying: those are good. And all together, they're worth about as much as a sesame seed, if what's inside you hasn't changed.
Pauri 21 opens with that list, and its sound is worth learning first.

teach.h: TEERATH — A FORD, A HOLY PLACE.
teach.b: Here is the opening line in the original: teerath tap daiaa dat daan. Five words, five practices. Teerath, TEE-rath: you know it from Pauri 6, the holy bathing place where Nanak said he'd bathe only if it pleased the One.
There it stood alone; here it leads a whole line. Tap, TUP, rhymes with cup: austerity, self-discipline, the word's root meaning heat. Daiaa: compassion, which we met in the bull stanza.
Dat and daan: gifts, giving, charity.
Said aloud, it rolls like a list: teerath, tap, daiaa, dat, daan.
The next line, in paraphrase: if anyone gains honor from these, it's only as much as a sesame seed. Til, the tiny seed. Not nothing.
Just small. Now, careful here. The stanza isn't mocking pilgrims or givers, and Sikhs themselves give generously and visit holy places, Harmandir Sahib in Amritsar most of all.
It's weighing where the real change happens.
The next lines say where, in paraphrase: the one who has listened, has trusted, and has loved in the mind has bathed at the pilgrimage place within. Hear the words coming back? Listening, suniai.
Trusting, mannai. And love. The words of Pauris 8 to 15 return all at once.
The real teerath is inside. Teerath tap daiaa dat daan: five good things, honored, and pointed inward.

how: Pauri 21 is recited in the morning Japji Sahib; many Sikhs give daswandh, a tenth of their earnings, and visit gurdwaras such as Harmandir Sahib, while hearing this stanza as a reminder that the inner change matters most.

o: a gift given freely to charity
a fast kept to discipline the body
a holy bathing place for pilgrims

games.q: the five of Pauri 21 — tap the pairs.

s: Pauri 21 says pilgrimage and charity are worthless
it says the honor they bring alone is small, a sesame seed, and points inward.
til, in Pauri 21, is a sesame seed
the honor good deeds bring on their own is the size of one tiny seed.
Pauri 21 brings back listening and trusting
the one who listens, trusts and loves bathes at the pilgrimage place within.

games.q: you've done it all: pilgrimage, fasting, kindness, charity. what does Pauri 21 say you've earned, on those alone?
o: honor the size of a sesame seed.
games.why: je ko paavai til kaa maan: honor like a sesame seed. the real bath is at the pilgrimage place within.

practice: Say the first line aloud slowly, teerath tap daiaa dat daan, five words like five steps, then twice more, and let it go quiet.
Think of one good thing you did this week; don't grade it, just ask gently whether it moved anything inside you. Rest with whatever answer comes, breathing.

wordCard.voice: Teerath, the holy pilgrimage place. It opens teerath tap daiaa dat daan: pilgrimage, austerity, compassion, gifts and giving, and points to the pilgrimage place within.

orig.note: Gurmukhi, Japji Pauri 21, line 1: pilgrimage, austerity, compassion, gifts and giving.

carryVoice: Your line: teerath tap. The real pilgrimage place, the stanza says, is the one within. Day one hundred ninety-five, done.
